core.title: Declare each train participant once as a typed participant id
core.given: A train definition (a plan artifact) whose actors — processing components, human roles, external systems and data sources — are declared as participants
core.when: The planner authors, edits or checks that train definition's participant declarations
core.then: List each participant exactly once as a typed participant id: one of the profile's participant-type prefixes (processing component, human actor, external system or data source) followed by its id, matching the profile's participant-id pattern.
prefer: Use the processing participant type for a component that performs processing, the human participant type for a human actor's role, and the external participant type for an external system or data source
Shape each id part according to the participant id-part syntax declared by the profile
avoid: Listing the same participant more than once
Using a participant type other than the profile's declared participant types, or omitting the type
An id part that does not conform to the profile's participant id-part syntax
Typing a human actor or an external source as a processing participant (or the reverse)
core.why: Train steps move artifacts between declared participants, so a uniquely named, typed actor list keeps every step's source and destination unambiguous and checkable.
evidence: Every entry in the train definition's participants list matches the profile's participant-id pattern
No participant string appears more than once in the list
Each participant's type matches its role: the processing type marks a component that performs processing, the human type a human actor, the external type an external system or data source
verification: Check every entry in a train definition's participants list against the profile's participant-id pattern; entries that do not match are findings.
Uniqueness is checked on exact participant strings: each participant is listed once, and exact string duplicates are findings.
The pattern check flags only entries outside the profile's pattern; id-part shapes the pattern still accepts (for example repeated or trailing hyphens where the pattern allows them) are not findings.

Whether a participant's type matches its actual role (processing component, human actor, external system or data source) is semantic evidence checked in review; the mechanical check covers pattern and uniqueness only.
Activation on file kind needs an observer that classifies plan artifacts as train definitions; scope is any such definition that is authored, edited or reviewed, whichever part of it changes.

fires: Planner authors a new train definition and lists its participants
Planner adds a processing component, human role or external source to an existing train's participants
Planner edits any part of an existing train definition (for example its steps) whose participant declarations must still conform
Planner or reviewer checks a train's participant declarations
doesNotFire: Editing a processing component's own internal artifacts without touching or checking any train definition
Code-level changes that do not touch planning artifacts

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds that the file_kind activation and the rule's scope refer to; in this stack, the workflow (train) definition kind.

The participant-id grammar of a train definition: the typed prefix for each participant type (processing component, human actor, external system or data source) and the id-part syntax, i.e. the combined validation pattern used by the obligation and its check.
profileRequirements.bunValue: wagon -> wagon:{wagon-id} (performs processing); user -> user:{role} (human actor); system -> system:{source} (external system/data source); validation pattern ^(wagon|user|system):[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$

proposedKeys.meaning: The grammar of participant ids in a workflow (train) definition: the typed prefix per participant type (processing component, human actor, external system or data source) and the id-part syntax, including the combined validation pattern.
proposedKeys.bunValue: wagon -> wagon:{wagon-id} (performs processing); user -> user:{role} (human actor); system -> system:{source} (external system/data source); validation pattern ^(wagon|user|system):[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: urn.<artifact> covers artifact URNs (component, acceptance, smoke_acceptance, train, wmbt, wagon, feature, journey) but no key carries the typed participant-id grammar of a plan artifact; the human-actor and external-system participant types have no artifact param, and the idiom group covers code constructs, not plan-artifact identifier grammar.

bunOnly.reason: The term/validator id of this rule's checker is a realization detail; the core's verification names the type check generically, and the type-to-pattern mapping it documents is carried by the profile key urn.participant.
Provenance pointer into the legacy ATDD-Bun convention tree; the neutral core keeps only the need for an observer that classifies plan artifacts as train definitions.

neutralityNotes: The concrete participant-id grammar — the type prefixes wagon:/user:/system: and the validation regex — is stack data with no existing vocabulary key, so it is carried by the proposed key urn.participant and the core speaks only of participant types and the profile's participant-id pattern. 'train' and 'participant' are ATDD-method planning vocabulary shared across stacks (the closed vocabulary itself lists train as an artifact param), so they remain in the core; the concrete plan-artifact kind name comes from roles.plan_artifact.kinds. 'wagon' as an actor type is neutralized to 'processing participant / component'. bun.json declares no severity, disposition or exceptions (unless is empty), so the core's verification adds none. The file-kind activation still needs a new observer; that gap is preserved verbatim.
